institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important thing when choosing UiT in Tromsø where their focus on arctic politic, society and history. Furthermore, it were important to me, that my study destination had a lot of opportunities in regard to nature experiences.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only bad thing about the exchange has been the exhausting and confusing application process, where it seems that UiT and UCPH have not agreed on how I should apply.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay easy to find the information, but to understand what I was suppose to do, was not

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. We found our housing on studenterheim, but we also looked at samskipnaden.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: My impression is that the social aspect takes up less space when you live off-campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Registration was easy, as an intro week was held for exchange students, where you could just turn up.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We attended the intro week where the registration was reviewed. We had to go to a website and accept/register for the subjects (and associated exams) we had been assigned and from there our schedule etc. created inside our personal page

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student counselor were available at the intro week

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful - I got all my first priorities

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take part in the intro week, meet your study counsellor and ask for help if you have any doubts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All of my courses were on MA level as I was told that I wasn't allowed to take BA courses when I was on exchange on my master.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was pretty surprised that there were no lectures and that most of my classes also were available online. But otherwise the teaching was a lot like UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Arctic Images
Quantitative Methods
Methods in Social Research

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't really think I can recommend any courses? Future exchange should pick courses of their interest?

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could do all kinds of sports at Kraft (UiTs sportscenter) and they also hosted different excursions, where you could meet other exchange students. Furthermore, the exchange team arranged different kinds of trips which where available on an app.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Nature experiences! Go hiking and skiing. Nature doesn't get much better than in Tromsø.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips to national parks or Svalbard if you have the time and money. Otherwise go to to Senja or Lyngen Alps!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The appreciation of nature and kindness of the locals

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Use "Tavla" to find academic activities 
2. Use 'Kraft' and 'Samskipnaden' to find social activities
3. Don't be afraid to ask the counselors for help with administrational stuff!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
My amazing and helpful professors who really taught me a lot academically about arctic history and politics. 
All the fantastic nature experiences I have had - both in the Troms region and on Svalbard.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Well, the admission and application proces.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
